canonical_facts.py.why: final_days, the canonical FINAL-day row reader: returns the stored row whole; its one caller (dsr.budget_plan.weekday_mix) reads sales, never the labor %

event_memory.py.why: event outcomes keep each night's HOURLY labor % (dsr_metrics labor.pct is hourly; the stored day is its fallback) so game nights are compared on one basis, beside the nightly report's hourly game labor

intelligence/dna.py.why: DNA reads the stored HOURLY day and adds the salaried share itself for a viewer who sees salaries (_labor_all_in); a login that may not see salaries reads `hourly` (profile(salaries=False))

intelligence/features.py.why: the cross-restaurant feature labor_pct_28d is HOURLY by design: cohort comparisons never carry one restaurant's salaries (INTELLIGENCE_ENGINE.md privacy rules)

intelligence/memory.py.why: busiest_days' labor_pct_by_day is HOURLY and read by nothing owner-facing: lines() names only the busiest and quietest days by sales

models.py.why: the figure's storage and its documented read: labor periods derived from the stored HOURLY days, get_labor_history (adds the salaried day share on read for a viewer who sees salaries) and the archive rebuild

schedule_economics.py.why: splh_objective sets the HOURLY record against the HOURLY target (the all-in target less the salaried share, _hourly_target_pct) — like with like, and the schedule budget stays hourly

schedule_intel.py.why: the schedule learners' week fingerprint (a TOTAL over the stored column) and the published week's daypart read — HOURLY punches over measured sales, never an owner-facing labor %

schedule_scorecard.py.why: the scorecard judges HOURLY labor % against the HOURLY target (_hourly_target_pct), and says so
